clue.text: Queen passes round one very old port

indicators.note: to pass round something is to encircle it, so the queen's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Alexandra was queen consort of Edward VII
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A queen's royal progress loops round a very ancient harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes round' puts I inside ALEXANDRA. The ancient Egyptian city, founded by Alexander the Great, was a great Mediterranean harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian city founded in antiquity was a major Mediterranean seaport.

parts.note: suggests a champion who has set many records, but means a container holding several gramophone discs

explanation.surface: An athlete holding several world records.
explanation.definitionFit: A book-like sleeve holding several gramophone discs, or a collection of tracks, holds many recordings.

clue.text: Invalid, or one sure to suffer disorder

indicators.note: to suffer disorder is to be thrown out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An ailing person is bound to fall ill with some complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' tempts as a sick person (IN-valid) but is the adjective meaning not valid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invalid is mistaken or unsound, wrong in fact.

clue.text: Sort of firearm religious group gives George

parts.note: an automatic is a self-loading gun
pi is short for pious, religious
a lot is a group or set

explanation.surface: A religious sect hands George a type of gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is RAF slang for an aircraft's autopilot. PI (pious) is a crossword staple for religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang named the device that flies a plane unaided after a person, George.

explanation.surface: Troops coming to a stop in their ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage that has pulled up and stopped, or soldiers arranged in ranks, fits both senses.

parts.note: a stall is a compartment, as in a stable or a shower

explanation.surface: Put something in a compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to put it in position.

parts.note: taken as written from the first part of the word
'not loud' is soft, and the musical marking for soft is p, for piano

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their buzzer made no great noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits 'wasn't' in two: WAS, then 'n't loud', read as 'not loud', giving P (piano, soft in music).
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging insect makes a buzzing drone as it flies, so it is a buzzer.

parts.note: added to the word poet, this flower forms the term for a second-rate versifier

explanation.surface: A bloom that diminishes a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A poetaster is a feeble poet: tack the flower onto POET.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy-like bloom of the Michaelmas daisy family is a flower.

clue.text: Church pieces inserted in some sort of paper

indicators.note: the two pieces are put inside the word for some

parts.note: some is a part of the whole
pieces in chess or draughts are men

explanation.surface: Bits of a church are tucked into a type of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some sort of paper' wants to be one phrase; 'some' is PART, and CH + MEN go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated animal skin for writing on, or paper imitating it, is a kind of writing material.

clue.text: Title Waugh took from history master's work

definitions.text: Title Waugh took from history master's work

parts.words: Title Waugh took from history master's work
parts.note: an Evelyn Waugh novel's name borrowed from part of the name of Edward Gibbon's great Roman history

explanation.surface: A novelist borrowing a title from a historian's masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbon's 'The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire' gave Evelyn Waugh his first novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's 1928 novel shares its title with Gibbon's history of Rome.

clue.text: A bitter exchange going over priest's head

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things around, so the letters of the two words change places

explanation.surface: A sharp argument flies right past a clergyman's comprehension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over priest's head' sounds like something the priest fails to understand; it is literally a hat worn on top of his head.
explanation.definitionFit: The square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy sits on top of the wearer's head.

explanation.surface: A heavy woollen top is making someone overheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper is a garment, and anything that makes a person perspire could whimsically be called a perspiration-inducer.

parts.note: the prefix meaning single or one
mania is madness or frenzy

explanation.surface: A peculiar kind of insanity is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession with a single idea or subject is a recognised form of mental disorder.

clue.text: Wood from poplar chosen — or regular chestnut

indicators.note: the wood is taken from within the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A timber picked from poplar, or perhaps the usual chestnut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or regular chestnut' is a nod to Monty Python's recurring joke 'And now... the Larch', a regular chestnut (old, well-worn gag); it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This deciduous conifer yields a durable timber, so it is a wood.

explanation.surface: A sturdy man who carries luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means stout in build, and porter was a dark beer from which stout developed.

parts.note: an extract is some of a text
The Times is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bit of the newspaper appears every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a newspaper: The Times. An extract is SOME of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally is the opposite of on every occasion.

explanation.surface: The finish on a French piece of furniture, perhaps, or a ballroom step.
explanation.definitionFit: The French feminine adjective for Polish is polonaise, and it is also a stately Polish processional dance.

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
an advance is a loan of money

explanation.surface: A mortgage arranged ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of time means before the event.

clue.text: This entertainment is much changed, everyone concludes

indicators.note: the piece for everyone comes at the end, concluding the answer
changed tells us the two words are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees this form of entertainment has altered a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns IS MUCH into MUSICH; ALL, from 'everyone', is placed last because it 'concludes'. Music hall was British variety theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre with comic songs and acts was a popular British entertainment.

clue.text: Endlessly attack holding, for example, spear

indicators.note: holding means containing the short form for an example
the last letter of the word for attack is dropped

parts.note: assail means attack

explanation.surface: A warrior attacks without end while gripping a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops L from ASSAIL to give ASSAI, which is 'holding' EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The light throwing weapon of southern African peoples is a spear.

explanation.surface: A printed page reports a small amount of plant development.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed handout is one sense; a small young plant leaf is the other.

clue.text: One direction given in a vessel

definitions.text: One direction given in a vessel

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: the compass point is put inside the container

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A command is issued aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes 'in' VAT after A; the whole clue also describes the word, a sailor's order to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: This nautical call to halt is an order issued on board ship.

parts.note: the cross-references read as 'occasions in entertainment', but the second answer is taken as music, so the clue means speeds or beats in music

explanation.surface: A bare pair of cross-references to other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down gives SOMETIMES, read as 'times', and 17 gives MUSIC HALL, read as 'music': times in music are its speeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the Italian word for musical speed, so these are speeds at which pieces are played.

clue.text: I'd act badly, turning up as revolting leader

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to a poor performance as a rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses IDHAM, which reads MAHDI. 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudanese religious leader who led a revolt against Egyptian and British rule was a rebel chief.

clue.text: Postpone as result of batsman's dismissal

explanation.surface: A cricket match is delayed because a batsman is given out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen; when one is dismissed, the stand is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a matter for later is to defer it, and a dismissal ends the batting partnership.

explanation.surface: A cursed person with a rosy complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' is a mild British euphemism for 'bloody', a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild British oath stands in for bloody, and a reddish glowing complexion looks healthy.

clue.text: Game John recollected in short publication

indicators.note: the rearranged name sits inside the shortened word for a periodical

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A man recalls something he read in a brief magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like 'remembered' but means collected afresh: HJON goes 'in' MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese tile game for four players is a game.

clue.text: Got to know so-called friends in court

explanation.surface: Discovering who one's legal allies really are.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts barristers refer to each other as 'my learned friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Got to know means acquired knowledge, and opposing barristers politely call each other 'my learned friend'.

explanation.surface: A naval manoeuvre on the officers' deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarterdeck' is read as quarter of a deck: a pack of cards has four suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four sets of thirteen cards is a quarter of the pack, and a lawsuit is a legal action.

indicators.note: to blend is to mix, so the letters of these two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A distiller experimented with a foolish mix of whiskies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend' sounds like whisky trade talk, but it signals rearranging TRIED SILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits such as Scotch are made in a plant where liquor is distilled.
